title: Enthalpy and Heat Capacity Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Beach sand burns your feet by noon but the sea stays cool. A steel pan gets hot in a minute but the water in it takes much longer. Same sun, same flame, so why such different speeds? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 5, Thermodynamics) Diya puts a pan of water on the stove and we find out.

You will see a sealed box (constant volume, q = ΔU) next to an open piston (constant pressure), meet enthalpy H = U + pV, and derive ΔH = ΔU + Δng RT step by step while counting gas moles on the molecule bench. Then heat capacity with steel and water on one flame (q = C ΔT = m c ΔT, water about 4.18 J per gram per kelvin), Cv and Cp for an ideal gas with Cp - Cv = R, and the bomb and coffee cup calorimeters. A worked NCERT style example finds ΔU for boiling water (41 kJ per mol gives about 37.9 kJ per mol). Then the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 53 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
